message.subject: Action required: your account will be suspended in 24 hours

signals.title: Reply-To points at a different organisation
signals.explanation: A reply would be delivered to recovery@mail-secure.example at mail-secure.example, not to micros0ft-login.example. Redirecting replies is how a conversation is moved somewhere the real sender cannot see it.
signals.advice: Check where a reply would actually go before responding.

signals.title: Sender domain resembles a known brand
signals.explanation: The sending domain micros0ft-login.example contains 'micros0ft', which reduces to the same confusable skeleton as Microsoft. micros0ft-login.example is not one of Microsoft's known domains, so the resemblance is not legitimate.
signals.advice: Treat as impersonation. Do not interact; escalate for analyst review.

signals.title: Display name claims a brand the domain does not belong to
signals.explanation: The display name claims Microsoft, but the message was sent from micros0ft-login.example, which is not one of Microsoft's known domains.
signals.advice: Treat the branding as decoration. Verify through the brand's own app or site.

signals.title: Message-ID domain does not match the sender
signals.explanation: The Message-ID was generated at mail-secure.example while the message claims to be from micros0ft-login.example. This is normal for mail sent through a service provider, so it only matters alongside the other findings here.
signals.advice: Corroborating evidence only. Read it together with the sender findings.

signals.title: Return-Path does not match the sender
signals.explanation: Bounces for this message go to mail-secure.example, but the reader sees micros0ft-login.example as the sender. Legitimate providers do this too, so weigh it together with the authentication and identity findings.
signals.advice: Check whether the envelope sender is an expected mail provider for this brand.

signals.title: DKIM signature is invalid
signals.explanation: DKIM reported result is fail for d=micros0ft-login.example. The signature does not validate. These results were reported by the receiving gateway and have not been independently verified.
signals.advice: The body or signed headers were altered, or the signature was never valid.

evidence.excerpt: mx.example.com; spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=bounce@mail-secure.example; dkim=fail header.d=micros0ft-login.example; dmarc=fail policy.p=none header.from=micros0ft-login.example
pass (mail-secure.example: domain of bounce@mail-secure.example designates 198.51.100.23 as permitted sender)

signals.title: DMARC failed or publishes no enforcement
signals.explanation: DMARC reported result is fail and the published policy is p=none. These results were reported by the receiving gateway and have not been independently verified.
signals.advice: Do not trust the visible From domain. Brand impersonation usually presents this way.

evidence.excerpt: mx.example.com; spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=bounce@mail-secure.example; dkim=fail header.d=micros0ft-login.example; dmarc=fail policy.p=none header.from=micros0ft-login.example
pass (mail-secure.example: domain of bounce@mail-secure.example designates 198.51.100.23 as permitted sender)

signals.title: SPF or DKIM passed for a domain that does not match From
signals.explanation: Authentication passed for mail-secure.example, but the message claims to be from micros0ft-login.example. The pass does not cover the identity a reader sees. These results were reported by the receiving gateway and have not been independently verified.
signals.advice: The pass authenticates a different organisation than the one being impersonated.

evidence.excerpt: mx.example.com; spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=bounce@mail-secure.example; dkim=fail header.d=micros0ft-login.example; dmarc=fail policy.p=none header.from=micros0ft-login.example
pass (mail-secure.example: domain of bounce@mail-secure.example designates 198.51.100.23 as permitted sender)

signals.title: Link uses an IP address as the host
signals.explanation: The link host is the IP address 198.51.100.23, not a domain name. Brands do not send customers to raw addresses.
signals.advice: Do not visit the address. Legitimate brands do not send customers to raw IPs.

signals.title: Anchor text disagrees with the link target
signals.explanation: The visible text names microsoft.com but the href points at 198.51.100.23.
signals.advice: Trust the href, not the painted text. Do not visit either without verifying.

signals.title: HTML attachment contains an external form or script
signals.explanation: The HTML attachment contains a <form>. The form submits to hxxp://collect[.]example/harvest. This is how a credential-harvest page is delivered without a link.
signals.advice: This is a credential-harvest page delivered as an attachment. Do not open it.
